title: Hederagenin ameliorates ferroptosis-induced damage by regulating PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 signaling pathway in HT22 cells: An in vitro and in silico study.
authors: Feng, Yuxin; Wang, Heran; Hu, Yazhuo; Zhang, Xiaoxue; Miao, XiuLing; Li, Zihan; Jia, JianJun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究常春藤皂苷元通过PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4通路抑制铁死亡，分子对接与动力学模拟仅用于小分子-蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hederagenin (HG), derived from ivy seeds, is known to offer protection against Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the specific molecular pathways through which it counters ferroptosis-induced neurotoxicity are not fully elucidated. This investigation seeks to delineate the processes by which HG mitigates neurotoxic effects in HT22 cells subjected to glutamate (Glu)-induced ferroptosis. METHODS: HT22 cell ferroptosis was prompted by Glu exposure. Cell viability was assessed using CCK-8 and LDH assays, while Fe(2+) fluorescence and assays of iron-related proteins served to gauge intracellular Fe(2+) concentrations. Evaluations of mitochondrial structure and functionality employed JC-1 staining and transmission electron microscopy. Assessments of ROS, lipid peroxidation, MDA, 4-HNE, and the GSSG/GSH ratio were conducted to ascertain HG's antioxidative efficacy. The expression of proteins within the PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 pathway was quantified via western blotting, with molecular docking (MD), and molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) used to explore protein interactions. RESULTS: HG diminished the cellular toxicity triggered by Glu in HT22 cells, lowered Fe(2+) within cells, and rejuvenated mitochondrial morphology and performance. Concurrently, it modulated proteins critical to Fe(2+) metabolism, diminished ROS and lipid peroxidation, and elevated GSH/GSSG ratios. Enhanced PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 protein levels were corroborated by western blot results. Furthermore, molecular docking revealed favorable binding of HG to the proteins PPARalpha, Nrf2, and GPX4, with binding energies of -7.751, -7.535, and -7.414 kcal/mol, respectively. MDS confirmed robust interactions between HG and these pivotal targets. CONCLUSION: The evidence suggests that HG effectively mitigates Glu-induced ferroptosis in HT22 cells by activating the PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 signaling pathway. These findings endorse HG's potential as a nutritional adjunct for AD management.
abstract_zh: 背景：常春藤皂苷元（Hederagenin, HG）源自常春藤种子，已知对阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）具有保护作用。然而，其对抗铁死亡（ferroptosis）诱导的神经毒性的具体分子通路尚未完全阐明。本研究旨在明确HG在谷氨酸（glutamate, Glu）诱导的HT22细胞铁死亡中减轻神经毒性效应的过程。方法：通过Glu暴露诱导HT22细胞铁死亡。使用CCK-8和LDH实验评估细胞活力，而Fe(2+)荧光及铁相关蛋白检测用于衡量细胞内Fe(2+)浓度。采用JC-1染色和透射电子显微镜评估线粒体结构和功能。检测ROS、脂质过氧化、MDA、4-HNE及GSSG/GSH比值以确定HG的抗氧化功效。通过蛋白质印迹（western blotting）定量PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4通路中蛋白质的表达，并使用分子对接（molecular docking, MD）和分子动力学模拟（molecular dynamics simulations, MDS）探索蛋白质相互作用。结果：HG减轻了Glu诱导的HT22细胞毒性，降低了细胞内Fe(2+)，并恢复了线粒体形态和功能。同时，它调节了Fe(2+)代谢关键蛋白质，减少了ROS和脂质过氧化，并提高了GSH/GSSG比值。蛋白质印迹结果证实了PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4蛋白水平增强。此外，分子对接显示HG与蛋白质PPARalpha、Nrf2和GPX4具有良好的结合，结合能分别为-7.751、-7.535和-7.414 kcal/mol。MDS确认了HG与这些关键靶点之间的稳健相互作用。结论：证据表明，HG通过激活PPARalpha/Nrf2/GPX4信号通路有效减轻Glu诱导的HT22细胞铁死亡。这些发现支持HG作为AD管理营养辅助剂的潜力。
